doc.title: Bill Kirchner interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2021

title: The best gigs: recorded concerts of his nonet and duo work
summary: Kirchner lists concerts that were recorded and released on CD, from the 1987 Chicago Jazz Festival to the 2014 'An Evening of Indigos'.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: No. I mean I worked, at the time there were these different club date offices that would just hire you and send you out to play with these ad hoc bands. Some of them were people that I worked with on a fairly steady basis and some of them were just one nighters, people I’d never seen before. But I would just go where I was told to go. But anyway, to answer the other part of your question, the best gigs I’ve ever done, I’m lucky in that several of them by serendipitously were recorded and have come out on CD. I mean one of them is doing the Chicago Jazz Festival in 1987 with my nonet and Sheila Jordan as a guest vocalist. I mean that’s on CD now. I sent you a link that that on YouTube. Another one is a concert that my nonet did at the Smithsonian in 1990 that is on a two CD set called “Trance Dance.” Yet another is a concert that the nonet did at the New School in 2001 that’s on CD, that’s called “Lifeline.” Still another is a duo concert that I did with Marc Copland at the New School in 2008, that’s on a CD called “Old Friends.” And then the last one is a concert at the New School in 2014 with Carlton Holmes on piano and Jim Ferguson is a great singer and bass player from Nashville and the late Holli Ross who was a wonderful singer who died a year or so ago of cancer, far too young by the way. So that’s on CD. That’s another thing called “An Evening of Indigos.” So I’ve been very lucky that some of the best nights of my career have been recorded well and are, and they came out great performance-wise, and they’re available on CD. So I’ve been exceptionally lucky in that respect.

I’m happy to hear that all the best gigs you mentioned were with your own arrangements and, you know, like sort of you being in charge. And I think that speaks well of your career also. A while back I watched a documentary on Quincy Jones. And you know I’ve been a fan, like most people, of the majority of his work and —
